items.front: In VPC peering, can instances in VPC B reach the internet through the NAT gateway of peered VPC A?
items.back: No. VPC B needs its own path to the internet.
items.extra: Resources in VPC B [can't use the NAT device in VPC A](../facts/vpc-peering.md#vpc-peering-edge-no-nat) to reach the internet.

items.front: In VPC peering, can you peer two VPCs whose IPv4 CIDR blocks overlap?
items.back: No. The peering connection cannot be created.
items.extra: You [cannot create a VPC peering connection](../facts/vpc-peering.md#vpc-peering-no-overlap-ipv4-ipv6) between VPCs that have [matching or overlapping IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR blocks](../facts/vpc-peering.md#vpc-peering-no-overlap-ipv4-ipv6).

items.front: VPC peering or a transit gateway: which one lets VPC A reach VPC C through a middle point?
items.extra: For peering, [transitive peering relationships are not supported](../facts/vpc-peering.md#vpc-peering-faq-not-transitive). When all attachments share the default route table of a transit gateway, [all attachments can route packets to each other](../facts/transit-gateway.md#transit-gateway-centralized-router-scenario).

items.front: In AWS networking, a partner VPC has the same CIDR block as yours and must call one of your APIs privately. Which service fits?
items.back: AWS PrivateLink, with an endpoint service for the API.
items.extra: With PrivateLink, consumer and provider VPCs [can have overlapping IP address ranges](../facts/privatelink.md#privatelink-wp-consumer-and-provider-may-overlap). The partner [creates an interface endpoint to your service](../facts/privatelink.md#privatelink-wp-provider-nlb-consumer-endpoint-steps).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, endpoint policy or IAM policy: which one can grant a role permission to read an S3 bucket?
items.extra: An endpoint policy [does not override or replace identity-based policies](../facts/vpc-endpoints.md#vpc-endpoints-policy-does-not-override-identity-or-resource-policies). The role still needs its own allow.

items.front: In AWS Transit Gateway, a VPC is attached and the transit gateway route table is complete, but instances cannot reach other VPCs. What is missing?
items.back: A static route to the transit gateway in the VPC route table.
items.extra: Transit gateway routes are not propagated to the VPC route table. The VPC owner [needs to create a static route](../facts/transit-gateway.md#transit-gateway-faq-no-propagation-to-vpc-route-table).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, servers in a data center must reach Amazon S3 privately over Direct Connect. Which endpoint type fits?
items.back: An interface endpoint for Amazon S3.
items.extra: Gateway endpoint connections [cannot be extended out of a VPC](../facts/vpc-endpoints.md#vpc-endpoints-gateway-not-extended-past-vpc). For access from a VPC in the same Region, AWS recommends [gateway VPC endpoints as they are not billed](../facts/s3.md#s3-faq-vpce-choose).

items.front: In VPC peering, the quota of active peering connections per VPC can be raised {{c1::up to 125}}.
In AWS Transit Gateway, one VPC attachment carries {{c1::up to 100 Gbps}} per Availability Zone in each direction.
In AWS PrivateLink, a VPC endpoint starts with a bandwidth of {{c1::up to 10 Gbps per Availability Zone}} and then scales automatically.
In VPC peering, data that crosses Availability Zones in one Region is charged {{c1::$0.01/GB in both "In" and "Out" direction}}.
In VPC peering, the count for a full mesh follows n(n-1)/2, so n = 100 needs {{c1::4,950 peering connections}}.
